title: Microsoft Purview: audit records for role and scoped-role permission checks
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap, Microsoft's supplied notice and the cited Learn documentation. It accurately separates the new operations from general Audit controls and leaves their undocumented licensing and record details open.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: General Audit licensing requires an appropriate organization subscription for audit-log search.
claims.quote: Licensing for Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium) requires the appropriate organization subscription that provides access to the audit log search tool

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: General Audit licensing includes per-user licensing needed to log and retain audit records.
claims.quote: per-user licensing that's required to log and retain audit records.

claims.claim: Audit retention and searchability depend on the subscription and the licence assigned to particular users.
claims.quote: The length of time that an audit record is retained (and searchable in the audit log) depends on your Office 365 or Microsoft 365 Enterprise subscription, and specifically the type of the license that is assigned to specific users.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions: retention
claims.claim: Audit (Standard) retains current audit records for 180 days.
claims.quote: In Audit (Standard), the system retains records for 180 days, which means you can search for activities that occurred within the past six months.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions: retention
claims.claim: Audit (Premium) defaults to 180 days for activities outside Entra ID, Exchange, OneDrive and SharePoint.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange, OneDrive, and SharePoint audit records are retained for one year by default. Audit records for all other activities are retained for 180 days by default

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions: retention
claims.claim: Applicable custom retention policies can change the default retention for other Audit (Premium) activities.
claims.quote: Audit records for all other activities are retained for 180 days by default or you can change the retention to a different duration using a custom retention policy.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions: retention
claims.claim: Audit records generated by non-user entities have a separate fixed one-year retention rule.
claims.quote: Audit records generated by non-user entities (such as service principal actions, system events, and application activities) are retained for a fixed period of one year.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Searching or exporting audit logs requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Admins and members of investigation teams must be assigned the View-Only Audit Logs or Audit Logs role in the Microsoft Purview portal to search or export the audit log.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Audit Reader and Audit Manager are the default role groups for the audit-search roles.
claims.quote: By default, the Microsoft Purview portal Role groups page assigns these roles to the Audit Reader and Audit Manager role groups.

claims.claim: Administrators restricted by administrative units can search and export only user-generated audit logs within their assigned units.
claims.quote: A restricted admin can only search and export user-generated audit logs within the scope of their assigned administrative units.

claims.claim: Unrestricted administrators can access all audit logs, including those from non-user and system accounts.
claims.quote: An unrestricted admin has access to all audit logs, including logs generated by non-user and system accounts.

claims.claim: An Entra role takes precedence at runtime over an overlapping scoped Purview role-group assignment.
claims.quote: If you assign both an Entra role and a scoped Microsoft Purview role group assignment to a user or group (for example, a role group scoped to an Administrative Unit), the Entra role takes precedence at runtime.

claims.claim: Administrative-unit scoping does not restrict effective permissions for the overlapping capabilities granted by Entra roles.
claims.quote: Entra roles always take precedence, and scoping applied through Administrative Units doesn't restrict the user's effective permissions for overlapping capabilities.

claims.claim: Audit logging is generally on by default for Microsoft 365 organizations.
claims.quote: Audit logging is on by default for Microsoft 365 organizations.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisite; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Business Basic, Business Standard and Business Premium do not enable auditing by default and require manual enablement.
claims.quote: Auditing isn't enabled by default for Small and Medium Business (SMB) licenses, including Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Business Standard, and Business Premium.

claims.claim: If auditing is off, Purview audit searches return no results.
claims.quote: When you turn off auditing, searches of the audit log in Microsoft Purview return no results. Running the Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell also returns no results.

claims.claim: Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled checks auditing status in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote:
To verify that auditing is turned on for your organization, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell:

Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled

claims.claim: The audit search is at Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search.
claims.quote:
Select the Audit solution card. If the Audit solution card isn't displayed, select View all solutions and then select Audit from the Core section.
3. On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <start> -EndDate <end> -Operations CheckUsersInRoles,CheckUserInRolesWithScopes uses valid parameters to filter the two notice-named operations.
claims.quote: The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation. The available values for this parameter depend on the RecordType value.

claims.claim: Activities - operations names accepts exact operation names for audit searching.
claims.quote: Activities - operations names: Enter the exact operation names to search for audited activities to include in your search results. You can enter one or more operation names, separated by commas.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog runs in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: The Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet is available in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Role groups are at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups.
claims.quote:
Go to Settings > Roles and scopes to view and manage compliance and governance roles in your organization.
2. Select Role groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity <role group name> -Member <user> adds a member with the role group's effective permissions.
claims.quote:
Add-RoleGroupMember
    [-Identity] <RoleGroupIdParameter>
    -Member <SecurityPrincipalIdParameter>

When you add a member to a role group, the member is given the effective permissions provided by the management roles assigned to the role group.

claims.claim: Viewing role groups in the Purview portal requires Global Administrator or Role Management.
claims.quote: To view Role groups in the Roles and scopes area in the Microsoft Purview portal, users need to be a global administrator or need to be assigned the Role Management role

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity enables auditing.
claims.quote:
Select the Audit solution card.

If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity.
4. Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true turns on tenant auditing in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote:
Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing.

Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: The start-recording banner is displayed when auditing is off.
claims.quote: If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity.

claims.claim: Learn documents turning auditing off through Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote:
Use Exchange Online PowerShell to turn off auditing.

Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $false

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Compliance Management and Organization Management hold the Exchange Online Audit Logs role by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Compliance Management and Organization Management role groups on the Permissions page in the Exchange admin center have this role.

claims.claim: Learn documents no setting specific to these two operations.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview CheckUsersInRoles CheckUserInRolesWithScopes ClientPortal licensing pricing configuration disable administrative units. Opened purview-permissions, audit-search and audit-log-enable-disable; no specific switch.

claims.claim: The change does not change ordinary users' experience.
claims.quote: There is no impact for organizations.
